newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends up vs spot dlr, slips in forwards.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends up vs spot dlr, slips in forwards.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended up at 35.8650/8750 against the dollar in Thursday's spot trade but slipped in the forward dollar market, dealers said.
"We saw a repetition of Wednesday's trend," said a dealer.
The spot rupee has tended to appreciate throughout this week as a leading Calcutta bank, which buys dollars on behalf of state-run companies, has stayed out of the market.
The spot dollar opened Thursday at 35.88/89 rupees.
"Some of the big corporates such as Reliance covered tidy amounts at 35.8650 level today," said a dealer.
The dollar saw a low of 35.8550 on Thursday.
The rupee saw some pressure towards the end of the day when the Calcutta-based bank bought small amounts at 35.8700/8750, dealers said. But the bank left the scene abruptly, they said.

One dealer wondered whether it was the absence of import demand or improved dollar supply that was keeping the rupee stable. Whatever the reason, it was a good sign for India Development Bond redemptions beginning next week, he said.
Forward premia edged up with six month annualised premia closing at about 7.6 percent, up from the previous close of 7.3 percent, dealers said.
The movement has been almost unidirectional after the announcement of January 20 state loan of 16 billion rupees late on Wednesday, dealers said.
Arun Dobey, director (foreign exchange) at Bank of America in Bombay said he considered the time most opportune for Indian exportes to receive premia and sell their dollars forward.
